Acquisition / Reach and engagement

Click-through rate (CTR)

The share of recorded ad impressions that generated a click, measured for one channel, placement, and reporting period. This measures attention before a visitor reaches your website.

Explore in the metric hierarchy ↗Open calculators →
Level 4Inspect the detail

The share of recorded ad impressions that generated a click, measured for one channel, placement, and reporting period. This measures attention before a visitor reaches your website.

%

How we use it

Compare creative variants within similar audiences and placements. We connect this view to landing-page conversion and qualified leads so attention can be evaluated alongside business outcomes.

Transparent calculationRecorded ad clicks ÷ recorded ad impressions × 100
clicks2,400
impressions120,000

2,400 ÷ 120,000 × 100 = 2%. Two clicks were recorded for every 100 impressions.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • Campaign and creative
  • Audience and placement
  • Device and market

Questions we investigate

  • Did audience or placement mix change?
  • Which relevant creatives attract clicks?
  • Do clicks progress to qualified outcomes?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Compare variants within similar delivery conditions.
  • Refresh relevant messaging and creative.
  • Review landing conversion alongside attention.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

Paid media lead
Weekly after enough comparable impressions accrue.

Required data

  • Consistent recorded click and impression counts
  • Campaign, audience, and placement identifiers
  • Reporting period and click definition

Read the measure with context

Zero impressions makes CTR undefined. An impression is not a unique person, and a click is not a qualified lead. Click definitions and acceptable rates differ across platforms and formats.
